Date: Tue, 07 Feb 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Indemnity for outputs — Gridlytics order form

Camila,

Thanks for the walkthrough this morning. As discussed, Gridlytics needs Redwood to accept responsibility for third-party IP claims that arise from outputs produced by Redwood models when those outputs are generated using Gridlytics prompts or customer-supplied content. In plain terms: if an external party alleges that text/code/images produced by the model (while called by Gridlytics) infringe their IP, we need Redwood to defend and indemnify Gridlytics for those claims.

A couple of clarifications so we're aligned:
- We are not asking Redwood to indemnify claims about the model's training dataset itself (i.e., not training-data indemnity).
- We expect a reasonable financial cap and a workable notice/defense process, but customer control over defense creates risk for us.

I've attached our redline of the Order Form (OrderForm_v2_redlines.pdf) and a short use-case summary (Proof_of_use_case.docx) to show the output types we're most concerned about.

Target timeline: we need a signed Order Form or an agreed path by 2028-02-21 to meet procurement windows. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept a carveout-style indemnity (narrowed scope) or if you need something different?

Jordan Price
Head of Procurement, Gridlytics
procurement@gridlytics.com

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. I've escalated the ask to Legal and copied Ben from AE so we can keep the commercial track aligned. Quick read: the request (defend & indemnify for model outputs produced using Gridlytics prompts/customer content) is material, and we should get Legal's recommended compromise before committing to anything.

Options we're preparing internally for you (high level):
- Narrow indemnity: Redwood indemnifies only where the alleged infringement is based on literal reproduction of customer-provided material (i.e., where the output matches a third party's content because that content was input by Gridlytics).
- Limited indemnity with escrow trigger/deductible: Redwood accepts indemnity but with a per-claim deductible and an escrow or insurance offset for large claims.
- Right-to-defend with customer control but Redwood reservation: default customer control with Redwood option to assume defense if necessary; CAP tied to fees.

Kimberly — can you review Gridlytics' redlines and advise on recommended language (scope + cap + defense control + notification/cure mechanics)? Ben, if Legal lands on a path we can accept, what's your preferred customer-facing framing (pilot/discount/contractual tradeoffs)?

I'll coordinate a three-way call (Gridlytics / Redwood Legal / AE) if that helps move to signoff.

Camila Reyes

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Feb 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Indemnity for outputs — legal view and proposed compromise

Camila / Ben — brief legal analysis and compromise proposal below after reviewing Gridlytics' redlines and the use-case doc. Summary: we should avoid an open-ended "model-output" indemnity but can offer a narrowly tailored indemnity that addresses the customer's commercial concern while protecting Redwood from indeterminate training-data exposure.

Proposed commercial/legal compromise (draft for redline):
1) Scope (narrowed): Redwood will indemnify and defend Gridlytics against third-party claims of infringement to the extent such claims arise from Outputs that: (a) materially reproduce or are verbatim copies of third-party content, and (b) were created by the Model in a manner that can be directly tied to Content supplied by Gridlytics or its End Users ("Narrow Output Indemnity"). Outputs that are solely the result of Model training or emergent behavior (hallucinations, probabilistic synthesis) are excluded.

2) Defense control / cooperation: Gridlytics will have the right to control the defense of any claim under the Narrow Output Indemnity. Redwood may assume control of the defense at its election, provided Redwood reasonably notifies Gridlytics and obtains the customer's cooperation. Both parties must cooperate and preserve privilege where applicable.

3) Financial cap: Cap per claim equal to the greater of (i) aggregate fees paid by Gridlytics to Redwood under the relevant Order Form in the prior twelve (12) months, or (ii) USD 500,000. This provides a commercially meaningful ceiling while tying exposure to commercial scale.

4) Deductible / trigger: Claims below USD 25,000 (per-claim) will be handled through reimbursement (i.e., Gridlytics to absorb costs up to the deductible). For claims above the deductible, Redwood's indemnity obligations will apply up to the cap.

5) Evidence & mitigation: Gridlytics must provide prompt written notice and reasonable evidence of the claim, and allow Redwood access to relevant inputs/outputs for technical remediation. Where feasible, Redwood may propose mitigations (filters, prompt constraints) as a condition of settlement.

6) Insurance/escrow: We can explore an insurance-backed option for expansion accounts — not required for initial Order Form.

Rationale: this addresses the customer's stated risk (outputs that reprint third-party content that the customer provided) while excluding broad training-data claims. The cap/deductible structure gives commercial predictability.

Next steps: I can prepare a redline (Indemnity_counterproposal_redline.docx) with the exact language. If AE wants, we can offer a limited commercial concession (pilot/discount) to close quickly.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

- Offer a 5% credit on first-year fees if Gridlytics accepts Redwood's right to assume defense (i.e., Redwood-step-in) to make the defense-control concession palatable.

Also recommend we schedule a 30-minute triage call with Gridlytics (include their CISO and procurement) this week to resolve open evidence and SOC2 requests. Here's a proposed time slot and a Teams link I use: https://teams.microsoft.com/l/meetup-join/example-slot (please swap if needed).
